problem_framing.rationale: Frames the decision exactly as posed (enter or not, and by which route) and scores A, B and J on the board's five stated objectives and constraints on one page. It identifies early what the answer turns on: Amazon ad cost for payback, and awareness-driven sell-through for retail. It also flags the ambiguity in "on the way to $40M" and states how it read it. Nothing material to fix.

storyline_coherence.rationale: Clear governing thought; the executive summary points map onto the sections; nearly every title is a claim its slide supports, and the titles alone give the argument. Flaws: the slide 3 title and decision 1 say only the Amazon-led route passes the investment, payback and margin tests, while the same scorecard shows Japan passing all three (the executive summary correctly says "only US route"). The slide 6 title asserts Amazon-first brands "lost far less", which its own evidence (revenue only) does not show. Some repetition across the executive summary, scorecard and decisions slide.

evidence_and_reasoning.rationale: I re-derived the unit economics ($10.73 / $4.73 / $4.01 / $7.55), Option A cumulative cash (−1.9, −1.8, −0.3, +2.4), the ACoS and duty sensitivity grid, break-even ACoS (28.6% / 26.9%), Option B cash (−20.8) and its four stress cases, group margins for all options, Japan cash, CAGRs and the 3.1× halo break-even. All reproduce within rounding; I found no numerical errors. All critical evidence is used, including evidence against the recommendation (32% benchmark, two stalled Amazon-first brands, slowing pilot growth, repeat below benchmark). The halo correlation is taken apart properly and B is shown to fail even with it. Weaknesses are small and caveated: competitor losses and Saebom's sequencing are over-read, and "volume matters less" is shown only at 25% ACoS in the body (the appendix shows payback fails at 28% ACoS with 90% volume). None changes the decision.

strategic_judgment.rationale: Recommendation is defensible and follows from the analysis: Amazon-led with a $4M envelope, ACoS, repeat and tariff guardrails, a redesigned retail gate (20% awareness, tied to the 4.0 delisting bar), an explicit reset of the $40M ambition, and Japan revisited in 2028. Alternatives are compared on the board's criteria and no trap is fallen into. Material flaw: the payback risk is under-resolved. Break-even ACoS is 28.6% against a 32% median for scaling brands, yet payback is called "likely on the planning inputs". The corrective trigger fires only above 30% for two quarters, where payback is already lost (−$1.0M). The proposed remedy of slowing growth to hold ACoS itself breaks payback on the document's own appendix (28% ACoS at 90% volume = −$0.6M). There is no fixed-cost lever, no explicit stop criterion beyond board review at the envelope, and the board is not asked whether it would relax the payback date.

clarity_and_concision.rationale: Answer is in the title, the executive summary and a one-page scorecard; language is plain and precise; the appendix states method and judgement calls transparently. Seventeen main slides plus appendix is slightly more than the decision needs, with the recommendation restated three times (slides 2, 3, 17) and the retail case spread over four slides.

unsupported_claims.why: The pack gives only revenue (below $5M) for Gaon Lab and Yeoreum and no loss or cash figures for any Amazon-first brand; their losses are inferred, not evidenced. Same issue with "the downside is a small business, not a $21M loss".

unsupported_claims.quote: Saebom added 300 doors in 2025 only after reaching ~$30M on Amazon.
unsupported_claims.why: The pack says about $30M of total US revenue in 2025 and doors added in 2025, the same year. It does not say the $30M was Amazon-only or that it preceded the retail entry.

unsupported_claims.quote: A national retail launch without awareness is the costliest way to fail
unsupported_claims.why: The pack does not report Mooncrest's awareness level or the cause of its delisting; attributing the failure to low awareness is an inference presented as the lesson.

unsupported_claims.quote: payback by end-2030 is likely on the planning inputs but not assured
unsupported_claims.why: "Likely" overstates. The document's own break-even is 28.6% ACoS against a pilot of 28% and a scaling median of 32% (range 26–38%); on that evidence payback by 2030 is at best a coin toss.

logical_contradictions.quote_a: Only the Amazon-led route passes the board's investment, payback and margin tests
logical_contradictions.quote_b: J passes the money tests but builds no US business.
logical_contradictions.why: The scorecard on the same slide shows Japan passing the cap, payback and margin tests, so A is not the only route that passes them. The executive summary's "only US route" is correct; the slide 3 title and decision 1 ("Only route that passes...") are not. A wording-level contradiction that does not change the conclusion.

recommendation.summary: Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon (Option A) with a $4M cash envelope and quarterly guardrails (ACoS ≤ 28%, repeat ≥ 29%, tariff re-plan). Decline the 600-door retail launch and make retail conditional on 20% awareness, >$10M Amazon sales at ACoS ≤ 28%, repeat ≥ 31% and a self-funding retail case, decided at end-2028. Restate the ambition as $25M+ in 2030 and $40M by 2032. Hold Japan in 2027 and revisit it for 2028.
recommendation.rationale: Meets all four defensibility criteria. It compares the options on the cap, payback and margin floor. It tests the 25% ACoS and 4.5 units/door assumptions against the benchmarks. It states the payback condition (ACoS ≤ ~28.5%, or 26.9% with a 25% duty) and the triggers. It says explicitly that $40M by 2030 is not reachable within the constraints. Weakness: the response to an ACoS overshoot is softer than the payback arithmetic warrants.

hypothesis_handling.rationale: Keeps the CEO's sequence (Amazon first, retail later) but modifies it on the evidence. The awareness trigger rises from 15% to 20% because the 10–20% band median (3.5) is below the 4.0 delisting bar. It adds ACoS, repeat and self-funding gates, replaces the fixed 2029 date with a gate decision, and resets the $40M date. It challenges the 25% ACoS, the 4.5 units/door and the 1.3× halo, and rejects the board member's correlation-as-cause. Payback uncertainty is flagged, though "likely" is generous. The one loosely supported causal or sequencing claim is that Saebom's retail came only after Amazon scale.

output.overall_comment: Top-tier analysis. Every figure I re-derived reproduces: unit economics, cash paths for all three options, the ACoS/duty/volume sensitivities, group margins, the B stress cases and the 3.1× halo break-even. All critical evidence and insights in the key are covered, no trap is fallen into, and the CEO's hypothesis is kept with well-argued conditions. What keeps it from a clean sweep: (1) the payback risk is identified precisely but handled a little softly — "likely", a 30% action trigger above the 28.6% break-even, and no reconciliation with the appendix showing that slower growth at 28% ACoS also misses payback; (2) a few over-read competitor inferences, including a slide title claiming Amazon-first brands "lost far less" with no loss data; (3) the "only route that passes" wording, which ignores that Japan passes the same tests; (4) modest repetition.
